source.title: No evidence for infants' contingency detection as a precursor of toddlers' self-recognition

confidence_rationale: A well-powered longitudinal null (N=113, two contingency measures at 6 and 9 months against four self-recognition measures at 18 and 26 months) is credible evidence against a necessary developmental route from action-outcome contingency sensitivity to self-representation. Confidence is held at the middle of the band because of mapping, not method: the outcome measure is explicit mirror/video self-recognition, whereas ARC-059 stage 1 posits an implicit self-versus-world attribution comparator. The null therefore bears on the ordering claim at one remove.
failure_signatures: Sensitivity to self-produced sensory contingency measured at 6 and 9 months did not predict any of four self-recognition outcomes at 18 or 26 months, so an architecture that treats contingency-based self-discovery as the developmental route to a self-model has no support from this longitudinal design.

If stage 1 competence is operationalised as a behavioural contingency-preference score, a downstream stage can improve with no measurable stage-1 predictor -- meaning a REE ablation that withholds stage 1 and then reads a self-model proxy may show no effect even when the ordering is genuinely load-bearing at the mechanism level.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Infants' contingency preference and contingency detection in the first year do not predict mirror or video self-recognition in the second and third year; self-recognition appears to emerge independently of contingency experience.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-059 stage 1 (self-as-object via motor experimentation) is asserted to be a precondition for the self-model that later stages require. The developmental analogue of that precondition -- contingency-based discovery of self-produced sensory change -- fails to predict the developmental analogue of the downstream self-model. On its face this weakens the load-bearing reading of the stage-1 gate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The translation is not tight in either direction. Mirror self-recognition is a conceptual, explicit self-representation of the kind REE does not implement and ARC-059 does not claim; stage 1's actual content is closer to an online egocentric body schema / self-world attribution comparator, which this study never measures. The contingency tasks are also looking-time preference measures, not measures of whether the infant has built an action-space model. So the study weakens a strong 'contingency experience is the route to selfhood' reading rather than the narrow comparator-precondition reading ARC-059 depends on.
mapping.source_context: Human infants, longitudinal, N=113; looking-time contingency tasks at 6 and 9 months; mirror-face, mirror-leg and video-face recognition at 18 and 26 months.

confidence_components.notes: Longitudinal design with a substantial infancy-standard N and multiple convergent outcome measures raises source quality above the typical infancy single-cohort study. Mapping fidelity is the limiting term: the construct measured downstream (explicit self-recognition) is a different level of self than the one ARC-059 stage 1 builds. Transfer risk is elevated because a null in human development does not establish that the ordering is dispensable for an artificial agent that has no innate action-space prior -- REE's stage 1 has to supply what infants may partly be born with.
